record.question: Childhood psychosis may include all the following EXCEPT
record.explanation: Source check: page 2 of the Paediatrics Technical Subject Paper-III (Oct 2022) prints Q11 exactly as in the bank with plain options (a) delusions, (b) loss of reality testing, (c) disorganized speech, (d) catatonic behaviour, with no underlining or italic emphasis on any option. Reasoning: the core manifestations of childhood psychosis are delusions, loss of reality testing and disorganized speech/thought disorder; catatonia is not a feature of childhood psychosis proper and in children is more commonly a manifestation of mood disorders, autism spectrum disorder or organic/neurologic illness, and when seen in childhood schizophrenia it tends to occur in older adolescents. Confidence is medium rather than high because DSM-5 lists 'grossly disorganized or catatonic behavior' among schizophrenia criteria, so a strict criterion-based reading could include it; the exam intent is nevertheless the option that is not a characteristic childhood psychosis symptom.
